summary: TTL field-type fix regression + live-DB type verification. All named writer sites confirmed writing real BSON datetime. All prior test suites still green (18/18 loop_safety + 196/196 cto_projects/PAT + 9/9 OAuth PKCE — 0 pre-existing failures observed, better than the 2-fail baseline main agent expected). Backfill script is idempotent (0 candidates on re-run). Naive/aware datetime stress test passes. HOWEVER: repo-wide TTL-field audit surfaced a MISS by the main agent — routers/loop.py:1081-1085 (cancel-fallback branch) still writes loop_sessions.updated_at as an .isoformat() STRING, and a live DB probe confirms loop_sessions.updated_at currently contains 42 datetime + 12 string + 8 float values (32% will never TTL-expire).

critical.issue: Writes loop_sessions.updated_at = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat() — a STRING. But loop_sessions.updated_at has a 365-day TTL index (init_prod_collections.py:312, expireAfterSeconds=31536000). MongoDB's TTL monitor only acts on BSON Date fields, so every cancelled-loop row written by this branch will sit forever. This is the EXACT same bug pattern the founder asked to fix repo-wide. Live probe: db.loop_sessions currently has 42/62 (68%) datetime, 12/62 (19%) string, 8/62 (13%) float in updated_at — the 12 strings match this writer site's fingerprint. Fix: change ts = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat() to ts = datetime.now(timezone.utc), then use ts.isoformat() only for the last_event.ts inner field if a string is desired there (or also switch it to datetime for consistency). Also add loop_sessions.updated_at to the backfill script scripts/fix_ttl_field_types_2026_08_27.py so the 20 already-broken rows get repaired.

action_items: FIX routers/loop.py:1081 — replace ts = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat() with ts_dt = datetime.now(timezone.utc); then set updated_at: ts_dt (datetime, not string). Optionally keep last_event.ts as the isoformat string if any consumer relies on it (or convert that consumer too).

EXTEND scripts/fix_ttl_field_types_2026_08_27.py to also convert loop_sessions.updated_at from string/float -> datetime. Currently that collection is NOT in the backfill list, so the 20 already-broken rows are permanent garbage until this is added and re-run with --apply.

Consider adding a CI/lint rule (or a codebase_health check) that flags any db.<coll>.insert_one/update_one where the value written to a TTL-indexed field is not a datetime object — this exact bug class has now bit the repo twice.

rca of the issue: Main agent's audit correctly found and fixed 4 writer sites and did a repo-wide grep, but the grep pattern missed the terminal cancel-fallback branch in routers/loop.py (lines 1077-1092) which is a rarely-taken code path that only runs when a user cancels while the engine is running. That branch was refactored earlier and still uses the old ts = ...isoformat() STRING pattern for BOTH loop_sessions.updated_at (TTL-indexed, real bug) and last_event.ts (harmless string display). The live DB confirms 12 rows already carry this bad-type value, plus 8 legacy float rows from a still-older code path. Reproduction: cancel a running loop; check db.loop_sessions.find({loop_id:'...'}).updated_at — it will be a string. Mitigation: change line 1081 to store a datetime, add loop_sessions.updated_at to the backfill script, re-run with --apply.
